name: yalsp
description: A standalone Ruby language server. No Ruby runtime required.

ya-lsp.serverPath.markdownDescription: Run a `ya-lsp` binary of your own instead of the one bundled with this extension — point it at `target/release/ya-lsp` to develop against a local build. Leave empty for the bundled one. `~` and `${workspaceFolder}` are expanded. Changing this restarts the server.

enumDescriptions: Also what was skipped or guessed — an unreadable file, a gem that could not be found.
Also what it did: which Ruby it picked, how many files it indexed, how long that took.
Also the work behind each request. Verbose enough to slow a large workspace down.
Everything, this crate and its libraries. For diagnosing the server itself.
ya-lsp.logLevel.markdownDescription: How much the server writes to the **ya-lsp** output channel. Read from the environment once, when the server starts, so changing it restarts the server. Left unset it does not override a `YA_LSP_LOG` inherited from your shell.

enumDescriptions: One line per request and notification: the method and how long it took.
The same, with each message's full JSON payload.
ya-lsp.trace.server.markdownDescription: Log the LSP traffic between VS Code and the server. For debugging this extension — to read what the server itself found, use `#ya-lsp.logLevel#`.

ya-lsp.gems.enabled.markdownDescription: Follow go-to-definition, hover and completion into the project's gems, read straight from `Gemfile.lock` and the gem directories on disk. Off, only your own code is indexed: startup is a little faster and every answer about a gem is missing. Overridden by `[gems] enabled` in a workspace `ya-lsp.toml`.

ya-lsp.gems.defaultGems.markdownDescription: Also index the ~40 gems that ship inside Ruby itself — `json`, `uri`, `forwardable`, `optparse`. Their directories under `gems/` are empty placeholders, so with this off `require "json"` leads nowhere and `JSON.parse` has nothing to offer. Overridden by `[gems] default_gems` in a workspace `ya-lsp.toml`.

ya-lsp.gems.rubyVersion.markdownDescription: Index the gems belonging to this Ruby, as in `3.3.0`, when detection picks the wrong one. Leave empty to read it from `.ruby-version`, `.tool-versions` or `Gemfile.lock`. Overridden by `[gems] ruby_version` in a workspace `ya-lsp.toml`.

ya-lsp.gems.paths.markdownDescription: Extra gem roots to search *before* the built-in table — each a directory containing `gems/`, which is what `gem env gemdir` prints. The escape hatch for a layout ya-lsp guesses wrong about: a container image, a Nix store path, a hand-rolled install. Relative paths resolve against the workspace folder. Overridden by `[gems] paths` in a workspace `ya-lsp.toml`.

ya-lsp.rbs.enabled.markdownDescription: Complete and hover `String`, `Array`, `Hash`, `Kernel` and the rest of Ruby's core, whose methods are written in C and appear in no Ruby source. Read from the `rbs` gem when one is installed, and from a copy inside ya-lsp when none is. Off, `"".upcase` has nothing to offer. Overridden by `[rbs] enabled` in a workspace `ya-lsp.toml`.

ya-lsp.rbs.stdlib.markdownDescription: Also the standard library — `CSV`, `URI`, `Logger`, `OptionParser` and ~57 others. Adds about 3.5 ms to every request, so turn it off on a very large project that only needs the core classes. Overridden by `[rbs] stdlib` in a workspace `ya-lsp.toml`.

ya-lsp.rbs.path.markdownDescription: Read signatures from this directory instead of looking for one — a directory holding `core/`, usually an unpacked `rbs` gem. Leave empty to find one automatically, falling back to the copy inside ya-lsp. Overridden by `[rbs] path` in a workspace `ya-lsp.toml`.

ya-lsp.types.guessFromNames.markdownDescription: Answer from a receiver's own name when nothing else can — `@user` is a `User`, `person` is a `Person`. The only answer ya-lsp gives that is allowed to be wrong: it is always labelled as a guess in the hover card and on a completion row, and it never displaces a type the code states or one derived from a signature or an assignment. Turn it off to keep only checkable answers. Overridden by `[types] guess_from_names` in a workspace `ya-lsp.toml`.

ya-lsp.diagnostics.enabled.markdownDescription: Show what ya-lsp finds while indexing in the Problems panel — files that do not parse, and constructs it could not follow. Off, nothing from ya-lsp appears there whatever `#ya-lsp.diagnostics.rules#` says. Overridden by `[diagnostics] enabled` in a workspace `ya-lsp.toml`.

enumDescriptions: Reported as a hint — a faint marker rather than a squiggle.
parse-error.markdownDescription: The file does not parse — Prism's own syntax error, and the only rule here that is unambiguously a defect in your code. **Default: error.**

enumDescriptions: Reported as a hint — a faint marker rather than a squiggle.
parse-warning.markdownDescription: Prism's warnings about code that *does* parse: `assigned but unused variable`, a duplicated `when`, a literal in a condition. Set this to `off` when RuboCop or Standard already reports them — `Lint/UselessAssignment` covers most of the same ground. **Default: warning.**

enumDescriptions: Reported as a hint — a faint marker rather than a squiggle.
dynamic-constant-reference.markdownDescription: A constant path ya-lsp could not follow, because what is left of the `::` is not itself a constant — `foo::Bar`. Legal Ruby; the rule records why go-to-definition stops there. **Default: off.**

enumDescriptions: Reported as a hint — a faint marker rather than a squiggle.
dynamic-singleton-definition.markdownDescription: `class << expr` or `def expr.name` where the receiver is not a statically known constant, so the singleton methods never enter the index. Legal Ruby. **Default: off.**

enumDescriptions: Reported as a hint — a faint marker rather than a squiggle.
dynamic-ancestor.markdownDescription: A superclass or a mixin argument that is not a constant — `class Foo < base`, `include mixin_for(x)`. Legal Ruby and ordinary in metaprogramming: on one real project this rule alone would have put 384 warnings on working code, which is why it ships off. **Default: off.**

enumDescriptions: Reported as a hint — a faint marker rather than a squiggle.
top-level-mixin-self.markdownDescription: `include self` or `extend self` written at the top level, where there is no enclosing module for `self` to name. **Default: off.**

enumDescriptions: Reported as a hint — a faint marker rather than a squiggle.
invalid-private-constant.markdownDescription: `private_constant` somewhere it cannot take effect: at the top level, on a dynamic receiver, or with a non-symbol argument. Mostly genuine misuse, but the last case is ya-lsp giving up rather than a defect — hence a hint. **Default: hint.**

enumDescriptions: Reported as a hint — a faint marker rather than a squiggle.
invalid-method-visibility.markdownDescription: `private`, `protected`, `public` or `module_function` used in a way Ruby does not accept: at the top level, with `attr_*` arguments, with an explicit receiver, or `module_function` inside a class. Also covers a non-literal argument, which is ya-lsp giving up rather than a defect — hence a hint. **Default: hint.**

enumDescriptions: Reported as a hint — a faint marker rather than a squiggle.
undefined-method-visibility-target.markdownDescription: `private :name` where no such method was indexed. A real bug once the index is complete, and off until it is: every hit measured across three real projects was `private_class_method :new`, which is correct Ruby that rubydex flags only because it does not model `Class#new`. **Default: off.**

enumDescriptions: Reported as a hint — a faint marker rather than a squiggle.
undefined-constant-visibility-target.markdownDescription: `private_constant :NAME` where no such constant was indexed. Off for the same reason as the method rule, and it also fires on a class whose superclass could not be resolved. **Default: off.**

enumDescriptions: Reported as a hint — a faint marker rather than a squiggle.

ya-lsp.diagnostics.rules.markdownDescription: How loudly each rule reports, keyed by the name shown in a problem's `code`. Only `parse-error` and `parse-warning` are statements about your code, and they are the only two on by default; the rest describe what the indexer could not follow, fire on legal Ruby, and ship `off` or `hint`. Set one to `off` when another tool already reports it. Overridden by `[diagnostics.rules]` in a workspace `ya-lsp.toml`.

ya-lsp.rubocop.hint.markdownDescription: Offer RuboCop's own extension once, in a project that has a `.rubocop.yml` or `rubocop` in its `Gemfile.lock`. ya-lsp never runs Ruby, so no cop offence and no autocorrect ever comes from it — RuboCop publishes a language server of its own, and it runs alongside ya-lsp rather than instead of it. Off, nothing is suggested and nothing else changes.

ya-lsp.index.include.markdownDescription: Globs, relative to the workspace folder, of the files to index. Everything ya-lsp knows about your code comes from these, so narrowing it is the quickest way to make navigation stop working. The default covers Ruby that is not named `.rb` — your `Rakefile`, `Gemfile`, `config.ru`, `lib/tasks/*.rake` and your own `.gemspec` — and the RBS signatures in `sig/`. Overridden by `[index] include` in a workspace `ya-lsp.toml`.

ya-lsp.index.exclude.markdownDescription: Globs to skip, applied after `#ya-lsp.index.include#`. Where vendored or generated Ruby goes when git does not already ignore it. Overridden by `[index] exclude` in a workspace `ya-lsp.toml`.

ya-lsp.index.loadPaths.markdownDescription: Extra roots to index and to resolve `require "..."` against, relative to the workspace folder — the `$LOAD_PATH` ya-lsp assumes. `require "foo/bar"` reaches `lib/foo/bar.rb` because of this. Overridden by `[index] load_paths` in a workspace `ya-lsp.toml`.

ya-lsp.index.respectGitignore.markdownDescription: Skip anything git ignores. Right for a code indexer by default — it prunes `vendor/bundle`, `node_modules` and `tmp` for free — but a project whose Ruby is generated into an ignored directory needs it off. Overridden by `[index] respect_gitignore` in a workspace `ya-lsp.toml`.

ya-lsp.index.maxFiles.markdownDescription: Refuse to index a workspace with more Ruby files than this, rather than thrashing. Raise it only after ya-lsp has said it stopped. Overridden by `[index] max_files` in a workspace `ya-lsp.toml`.
